Applying for PGT & PGR Study
at Durham University
Postgraduate Admissions
October 2024
PGT Dates and Deadlines
• The admissions cycle opens at the beginning of October each year for
entry in the following September/October
• The current application deadlines are:
➢ 31 July 2025 for applicants who will require a student visa
World Top
➢ 31 August 2025 for applicants who will not require a student visa 100
• Please apply early if possible as some courses may close to Ranked 89th in the
admissions if they become over-subscribed QS World University
Rankings (2025)
• A few courses may also have earlier deadlines which will be advertised
on the relevant academic department webpages, eg MSc Management
programmes
The PGR Admissions Cycle
• The cycle normally opens on 1st October each year
• Intakes for departments vary – October/January/April starts
• Most programmes have no official application deadlines (any deadlines World Top
will be clearly stated on relevant academic department web pages) -
but applicants must consider admissions decision and processing
turnaround times, especially if a student visa is required
100
• Encouraged to apply early if possible Ranked 89th in the
QS World University
• PGR applications are submitted to the Applicant Portal and considered Rankings (2025)
by the department, with Admissions issuing the decision
Staged Admissions
• The following courses operate a staged admissions process:
➢ Full-Time MBA
➢ MSc Business Analytics
➢ MSc Marketing
➢ MSc Scientific Computing & Data Analysis (Computer Vision &
Robotics)
➢ MSc Conservation of Archaeological & Museum Objects
• These courses have application deadlines throughout the
admissions cycle with multiple rounds of applications
Course Search and How to Apply
• Search our courses on our website, either on academic department webpages at
Academic - Durham University or the course search functionality at Study - Durham
University
• Look at the relevant Entry Criteria for your chosen course
• Open the Application Portal at Home · Application Portal (microsoftcrmportals.com)
and create an account
• Use the course search option in the portal to locate the course you want to apply for,
select the academic year (2025/26 for courses starting in September 2025,
or 2024/25 for any PGR courses prior to this), mode of study (full-time or part-time)
and click on Apply
• Complete all sections of the application form and click on Submit (or Save it and
submit later)
Entry Criteria
• Academic requirements:
➢ For PGT normally an upper second class (2:1)
Bachelor degree or international equivalent
➢ For PGR normally a Masters degree or international
equivalent
➢ Some courses will have degree subject and/or module
requirements
➢ International Office set international equivalencies
• English language requirements
➢ Direct entry and pre-sessional entry requirements
➢ UKVI SELT may be required (if pre-sessional only
CAS needed)
➢ English Language Requirements - Durham University
• Personal statement or research proposal for PGR
• References (if required)
• Programme specific requirements, eg interview
or relevant experience
Application Fee
• There is a £60 application fee for all Business School
MSc programmes
• After submitting your application, you will receive an
action request in your portal asking you to pay the
application fee
• We will not consider your application until the fee has
been paid
• You can only pay and be considered for one
programme per programme suite
Application Portal
• Apply at Home · Application Portal
(microsoftcrmportals.com)
• View all applications either started or submitted
• View application status
• View action requests and notifications
• Raise an enquiry
• View offer
• Accept offer
• Upload documents
• Apply for a pre-sessional English language course
(if eligible)
• View and approve CAS details (if required)
Types of Application Decisions
• Unconditional Offer
• Conditional Offer
➢ Academic
➢ English Language (inc pre-sessional)
➢ References
➢ Other
• Unsuccessful Decision
• Invite to Interview
• Further Information Required
Pre-Sessional English Language
• 6 / 10 / 20-week courses all offered on-campus in 2025
• Must be stated as an offer condition on your offer letter in
order for you to be able to apply (or unconditional)
• Pre-sessional English eligibility requirements are on our
website at Pre-Sessional English Language Required -
Durham University
• Apply via the application portal
• Must pass in order to progress to your main Masters
programme
CAS
• Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies
• Enables international applicants to apply for their student visa
• In order to be eligible for a CAS:
➢ Accept offer
➢ Pay deposit (if required)
➢ No outstanding offer conditions
➢ Documents must meet UKVI guidelines (eg translations)
➢ Can only issue CAS 5 months before programme start date
• Combined CAS possible if English Language is the only outstanding offer
condition and applicant accepted onto a pre-sessional English language
course
• UKVI SELT will be required if pre-sessional only CAS is needed
Academic Technology Approval Scheme (ATAS)
• Linked to national security & anti-terrorism legislation
• Mandatory requirement within immigration rules for students intending to enter or remain in the UK
• Students who require ATAS will not be able to register onto their programme without it
• Affects applicants planning to undertake a degree in some science, engineering or technology
disciplines
• If offered a place and ATAS is required, the offer letter will include CAH3 code and ATAS statement
of purpose
• Applicants apply online for an ATAS clearance certificate at the Foreign and Commonwealth Office
website
• Admissions are unable to expedite this process
Admissions Process
PGR only:
• Contact the academic department of the programme you would like to apply for
to register and discuss your research interests and to explore potential supervisor
availability
• Visiting Research students need to apply and are considered in the same way
Application Considerations:
• For PGT, the PG Admissions Team consider applications in close liaison with
academic departments
• For PGR, academic departments consider applications
Admissions Process
After Applying:
1. Receive Interview Invite attend interview 2, 3, or 4 below
OR
2. Receive Unconditional Offer (see over)
OR
3. Receive Conditional Offer (see over)
OR
4. Receive Unsuccessful Decision End
OR
5. Receive Action Request asking for Further Information provide requested
information/documentation 1, 2, 3 or 4 above
Admissions Process
2. Receive Unconditional Offer
• Accept Offer in Portal
• Pay Deposit (if required)
• College membership/accommodation
• CAS/Visa (if required)
• Online Enrolment
• Arrive
Admissions Process
3. Receive Conditional Offer
• Accept Offer in Portal
• Pay Deposit (if required)
• College membership/accommodation
• Meet offer conditions
➢ Apply for pre-sessional English course if required
• CAS/Visa (if required)
• Online Enrolment
• Arrive
Funding
• For PGR this will vary from department to department – contact your department
directly to check what funding opportunities may be available
• The Business School offers scholarships automatically for strong PGT offer holders
• There are further scholarship/funding opportunities listed at Postgraduate
Scholarships Durham University
• Further information can be provided by our Scholarships team at
scholarships.advice@durham.ac.uk
